sources.citation: Bee, Darlene. 1965. Comparative and historical problems in East New Guinea Highland languages. Pacific Linguistics A-6: 1-38.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Marks stress on Tairora forms from Vincent's lexical list without a placement statement (per nort2920 check); bibliography lists Vincent & Vincent 1962 'Tairora Phonemic Statement' TS (unpublished).

sources.citation: Vincent, Alex R. 1962. Notes on Tairora noun morphology. Work Papers of the SIL, University of North Dakota Session 6: 21-46 (Article 9). DOI 10.31356/silwp.vol06.09.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 21 (image-only scan, read on page image): phoneme paragraph ends 'Stress is left unmarked in this paper.' Data from Bantura village = North Tairora.

sources.citation: OLAC, 'resources in and about the South Tairora language' (Internet Archive copy 2024-12); transnewguinea.org 'Tairora, South' lexicon (source 'SIL (1976)').
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: OLAC lists no phonology item for omw (dialect survey, primer, McKaughan 1963, Crubadan, transnewguinea.org). transnewguinea.org wordlist carries unexplained acute accents on a few forms (tánturu 'axe', múkiari 'bone', ándere 'cold').

sources.citation: Vincent, Lois E. & Anisi Kaave. 2010. Tairora-English Dictionary (full, viii+642 pp., grammar appendix pp. 576-608).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent: no stress statement; p. 578 notes vowel length and two lexical tone contrasts (per the nort2920 check). Obura forms appear only as dialect variants of headwords.

sources.citation: Vincent, Lois E. & Anisi Kaave. 2010. Tairora-English Dictionary, Preface/Introduction pp. iv-viii ('The sounds of Tairora'). Ukarumpa: Wycliffe/SIL. SIL archives entry 52860.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress. p. iv lists the North/South dialect differences (4- vs 5-way verb distinction; nr and mw phonemes only in the South; animacy in 'to be'); entries are North Tairora (Suwaira).

sources.citation: SIL PNG Branch (data checked by Alex & Lois Vincent 1992, 1994). 2011 [printed 7 Sept 2004]. Organised Phonology Data: Tairora [Northern] Language [TBG], Kainantu, Obura, Eastern Highlands Province. 3 pp. Draft ms., SIL archives entry 42240.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 2 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)': 'Stress is often, but not always, connected with the high tone. High tone is phonemic.' p. 3: 'This is the orthography for Northern Tairora only.. Tone or stress is not.' No placement rule. Header lists northern and southern villages and 13,500 speakers, but the inventory (no nr, mw) and the orthography note make it North Tairora [tbg] = nort2920 (a new find for that target).

sources.citation: Vincent, Alex & Lois Vincent (compilers). 1994 [data checked Sept 1992, 1994; printed 7 Sept 2004]. Organised Phonology Data: Tairora [Obura-To'okena dialect] Language [TBG], Obura, Eastern Highlands Province. Ukarumpa: SIL PNG Branch. 4 pp. Draft ms., SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 42525.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 3: the heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' is followed directly by 'Syllable Patterns' (section left empty; verified on the page image); under 'Conventions: Orthographic' only 'Tone or stress is not.' No placement statement. This is the South Tairora (Obura-To'okena = Omwunra-Toqura) dialect although SIL files it under tbg.

sources.citation: McKaughan, Howard. 1973. Introduction [to Part Four: Tairora-Binumarien-Waffa]. In H. McKaughan (ed.), The Languages of the Eastern Family of the East New Guinea Highland Stock, 515-516. Seattle: University of Washington Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: pp. 515-516: 'The Vincents, in an unpublished manuscript (1962c), list the consonants of Tairora . Word prosodemes of stress are postulated rather than tones as in the other languages, though Stringer and Hotz describe stress for Waffa too. The relation between stress and tone in these languages is intimate.' Second-hand, dialect unspecified (Vincents' data = North Tairora), no placement. Table of contents shows no Tairora phonology chapter; Kerr's Obura chapter (598-624) is verb morphology.

sources.citation: Vincent, Alexander. [1957-2003] (Glottolog 2015). Dialects of the Tairora Language of the Eastern Highlands of Papua New Guinea. Ms., 147 pp. SIL archives entry 63951, attachment 2.19 MB).
